also: get it over and done with

evidence: Cato Agr. 2.1: satisne temperī opera sient cōnfecta
Verg. G. 2.541: sed nōs immēnsum spatiīs cōnfēcimus aequor

terms.comment: Of finishing a thing well: Lewis & Short sets absolvere apart from it, as “without denoting intrinsic excellence, like perficere”.
Lewis & Short: “to bring a work to a close, to complete, finish”, probably from taking a finished web off the loom.

phrases.latin: vīlicum vocet, roget quid operis siet factum, quid restet, satisne temperī opera sient cōnfecta, possitne quae reliqua sient cōnficere
phrases.english: Let him call the farm manager and ask what work has been done, what is left, whether the jobs were finished in good time, and whether he can finish what remains.

phrases.latin: aliud est properāre, aliud festīnāre. quī ūnum quid mātūrē trānsigit, is properat; quī multa simul incipit neque perficit, is festīnat
phrases.english: Hurrying is one thing, rushing another: whoever finishes one thing promptly is hurrying; whoever starts many things at once and finishes none is rushing.

phrases.latin: Tarquiniōs rēgēs ambōs patrem vōvisse, fīlium perfēcisse
phrases.english: both Tarquin kings: the father vowed it, the son completed it
